messages:
Emma: After upgrading redwoodctl to v0.12.3 I'm stuck in an auth refresh loop when working from my corp laptop behind an HTTP proxy. It keeps opening the browser and then showing 'Callback failed: token_exchange_error'. Logs:

[ERROR] auth: refresh token failed: 401 invalid_grant
[INFO] spawning local callback at http://127.0.0.1:42311/callback
[INFO] opening browser...
[ERROR] callback: get http://127.0.0.1:42311/callback: dial tcp 127.0.0.1:42311: connectex: No connection could be made

Anyone seen this? :facepalm:

Joon: Do you have HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY set? Corporate proxies (NTLM) often break local callback flows. Also are you using the OS keychain/credential manager?

Emma: Yes, both HTTP_PROXY and HTTPS_PROXY are set (http://proxy.corp:8080). Using macOS Keychain (redwoodctl stored token there). Repro: 1) `redwoodctl login` (opens browser) 2) redirect sometimes returns 502 or "connection reset by peer" 3) CLI keeps attempting refresh and fails repeatedly.

Priya: Can you paste your profile (~/.config/redwood/profiles.yaml) with sensitive bits redacted?

Emma: Sure (sanitized):
```
profile: work
auth:
  method: browser
  use_system_keychain: true
proxy:
  http: http://proxy.corp:8080
  no_proxy: localhost,127.0.0.1
```

Carlos: Weird — `no_proxy` should cover localhost callback, but some corporate transparent proxies still intercept. Quick tests: try `unset HTTP_PROXY HTTPS_PROXY` before login so the browser callback hits localhost directly.

Emma: Unsetting proxy before login makes the browser flow succeed once, but after a few minutes redwoodctl's token refresh goes out and hits the corp proxy and dies. Workaround I found: `REDWOOD_USE_OS_KEYCHAIN=false redwoodctl login --headless` and paste the token — that persisted for hours.

Joon: If `--headless` exists in your CLI version, that's the recommended flow behind proxies. It avoids local callback entirely. If it's not present, we need a guard. I'm filing a ticket. Also try `NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1` exported in your shell; some OS/proxy stacks require that env var name.

Emma: Headless flag isn't in v0.12.3 (I only have `--no-open`). I opened a repro and attached logs: https://ourtracker/DEVEX-789 — steps and the log snippet are there.

infra-bot: Ticket DEVEX-789 created and assigned to @Joon.

Joon: I'll add a check in the login flow to detect HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY and either prefer headless or print a clear warning with a one-line workaround. For now: 1) delete any stored keychain entry (`security delete-generic-password -s redwood-token` on macOS), 2) unset proxy envs, 3) run `redwoodctl login`, 4) re-export proxy envs and ensure `NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1` is set. Alternatively you can use `redwoodctl auth token create --ttl 24h --profile work` to mint an ephemeral token if your account allows it.

Emma: Confirmed `REDWOOD_USE_OS_KEYCHAIN=false` + `redwoodctl auth token create` worked for me. I'll update our internal onboarding notes with a short section on corporate proxies and the login flow.

Priya: :raised_hands: I'll add an auth caveats subsection to docs/quickstart about proxies/keychain quirks and link to DEVEX-789 for the fix.

Carlos: Thanks for reporting — this has bitten a few folks. We'll aim for a clear UX patch in the next CLI release. :thumbsup:
